concepts.name: Three-Dimensional Objects
concepts.description: Three-dimensional (3D) objects have length, breadth, and height. Students observe common solids such as cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, and spheres in everyday life.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify common three-dimensional objects and describe their basic characteristics.

concepts.name: Faces, Edges, and Vertices
concepts.description: Every solid has flat or curved faces, edges where faces meet, and vertices where edges intersect. These features help distinguish different solids.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the faces, edges, and vertices of common three-dimensional solids.

concepts.name: Real-Life Examples of Solids
concepts.description: Students relate geometric solids to familiar objects such as boxes, cans, balls, and ice-cream cones to strengthen spatial understanding.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to match everyday objects with their corresponding three-dimensional shapes.

concepts.name: Top, Front, and Side Views
concepts.description: A three-dimensional object appears different when viewed from the top, front, or side. Students learn to recognize these different perspectives.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the top, front, and side views of simple three-dimensional objects.

concepts.name: Observation and Visualization
concepts.description: Students develop spatial visualization by imagining how objects appear from different viewpoints without physically moving them.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to visualize and describe objects from different viewing angles.

concepts.name: Comparing Different Views
concepts.description: Different views provide unique information about the same object. Comparing these views helps in understanding the complete structure of a solid.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to compare different views of a three-dimensional object.

concepts.name: Drawing Simple Sketches
concepts.description: Students create freehand sketches of cubes, cuboids, cylinders, and other solids by observing their visible faces and edges.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to draw simple sketches of common three-dimensional objects.

concepts.name: Visual Representation
concepts.description: Sketches help represent three-dimensional objects on two-dimensional paper while maintaining their overall appearance.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to represent simple solids through accurate sketches.

concepts.name: Building Spatial Reasoning
concepts.description: Drawing and interpreting sketches improve students' ability to mentally manipulate and understand three-dimensional objects.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to use sketches to visualize and interpret three-dimensional shapes.

concepts.name: Nets of Solids
concepts.description: A net is a two-dimensional pattern that can be folded to form a three-dimensional solid. Students explore simple nets of cubes and cuboids.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify and recognize simple nets of common solids.

concepts.name: Constructing Solids
concepts.description: By folding paper nets, students understand how flat shapes combine to create three-dimensional objects.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to construct simple three-dimensional solids using paper nets.

concepts.name: Applications in Daily Life
concepts.description: Packaging boxes, cartons, gift boxes, and containers are practical examples of solids formed from nets.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to relate nets of solids to packaging and other real-life applications.

concepts.name: Understanding Boxes and Sketches
concepts.description: This chapter develops students' spatial reasoning through the study of three-dimensional objects, different viewpoints, sketches, and simple nets of solids.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify, sketch, visualize, and interpret common three-dimensional objects from different perspectives.
